schema: genre -> roles -> targets; each target: dna (v2, canonical), recipe (one-line ASCII), v3_dna and features, windows/library sounds used and alternates, sndrec_feel, edition badge, ships, priority, pack
checks: Every dna and v3_dna was parsed by core/dna.cpp parse() on main (library catalogue loaded) and by design/v3 canonical3() on preset-engine-2: no unknown NAME, no empty layer, at most 1024 bytes; stored in canonical form. Every recipe is design/v3 toRecipe(OneLine) and parses back (fromRecipe) to the same canonical DNA. K is computed from the measured root of the first key-tracked layer (windows-sounds.json, library note names), other tonal layers get T to the nearest octave. Nobody has listened to them yet.

genres.name: Deep house
genres.keys: Minor keys (A, F, D, E minor); minor 7th and 9th voicings, two-chord vamps; maj7 colour
signature: minor 7th/9th organ or e-piano chord stabs on the off-beat, often with a dotted-8th delay
round sine or nearly-sine sub bass following the chord roots in two-bar lines
soft hats and shakers with swing, rim shots, a muted clap
short spoken or sung vocal fragments, filtered
warm, low-contrast pads; filter sweeps as the main FX
genres.producer_wants: Chords that sit (no energy below ~100 Hz so the bass has room), a bass that is felt more than heard, presets that are ready to swing, and macro filter sweeps.
genres.sndrec_feel: Let Sound Recorder echo (E) be the dub delay on the stabs and keep the stab short with a hard Delete After: the cut edge is the click of a gated sampler. Keep XP's marimba ding audible as the tine.

sources.title: Native Instruments blog: How to make a deep house track

genres.name: Classic (Chicago) house
genres.keys: Major and minor; piano riffs on I-IV or vi-IV-V; organ and piano stabs in root position
signature: house piano chords (a bright rompler piano, root plus octave)
squelchy 303-style acid lines (acid house) or a punchy organ/rompler bass
drum-machine kits: 909 kick and hats, 808/909 clap
orchestra hits and string stabs from ROMs
genres.producer_wants: Instantly playable piano/organ stabs that cut through, raw drum machines, and an acid line with accent and slide.
genres.sndrec_feel: Use the 3.x CHORD.WAV as the struck house-piano chord and TADA as the stab: they are period-correct ROM-age samples already.

sources.title: Sound on Sound: Secrets of House & Trance (2004)

genres.name: French house (filter house)
genres.keys: Major-key disco loops; 7th and 9th chords lifted from 70s/80s funk and disco
signature: a filtered disco sample loop that opens and closes (the filter IS the arrangement)
genres.producer_wants: Loop-like chord stabs with a phaser sweep, funky basses, a talkbox-like vowel lead, and a pump they can feel without a compressor.
genres.sndrec_feel: Make the pump a drawn amplitude envelope (Ja) per beat; make the phaser a SELF-FLANGE (C@3X) baked into the buffer, so the strip shows the comb.

genres.name: Detroit techno
genres.keys: Minor and modal (Dorian, Aeolian); string-pad chords with sus and minor-7 colour
signature: lush, futurist string pads and chords
TR-909 drums with claps and open hats
genres.producer_wants: Soulful pads and stabs over machine drums; sequences that groove; an optimistic, space-age tone colour.
genres.sndrec_feel: The XP startup is literally a futurist string swell: slow it, unison it, and let its four-note figure come through when the macro opens.

genres.name: Minimal techno and microhouse
genres.keys: Often atonal or one-note; when tonal, minor and static
signature: clicks, ticks and very short percussive blips
tiny metallic hits and wooden perc
genres.producer_wants: Perfect, tiny one-shots: clicks with pitch, wooden and metallic perc, short sub hits. Space between sounds matters more than size.
genres.sndrec_feel: This is Sound Recorder's home ground: the shortest Windows sounds (menu, xpstart, infobar, balloon) are already minimal-techno percussion. Present them nearly raw.

genres.name: Dub techno
genres.keys: Minor; one chord (minor or minor-7) for minutes
signature: a single chord stab drenched in tape delay and reverb, filtered over minutes
genres.producer_wants: A chord stab with a long, evolving delay tail; a hiss bed; space.
genres.sndrec_feel: Dub delay is exactly what layer offsets plus Sound Recorder echo give: each tap is a real recorder starting later, each echo a real Add Echo.

genres.name: Trance
genres.keys: Minor keys, epic i-VI-III-VII progressions; anthem breakdowns
signature: supersaw leads and chords (seven detuned saws)
genres.producer_wants: Wide, bright supersaws; 1/16 trancegate patterns; plucks with tempo delay; risers that build over 8-16 bars.
genres.sndrec_feel: The fanfare (TADA) is the supersaw: sustain it with LOOP-OSC and spread it with U7. Draw the trancegate as an amplitude envelope; keep its steps on the 1/16 grid.

genres.name: Drum and bass and jungle
genres.keys: Minor; bass carries the harmony; often one key centre (F, E, G minor)
signature: chopped breakbeats (the Amen and other funk breaks), time-stretched and pitched
reese bass (two detuned saws, slow beating), and sub
jungle: sound-system sub and dub sirens, ragga vocal stabs
genres.producer_wants: A reese that moves on its own; deep sub; breaks that can be chopped and pitched; atmos pads for liquid.
genres.sndrec_feel: The XP ringback tone is two sines that already beat: that is the reese motion for free. For breaks, the kit strip (v3) is literally a chopped break in one buffer.

genres.name: UK garage and 2-step
genres.keys: Minor 7th and 9th chords; R&B harmony; organ bass on roots
signature: skippy 2-step drums (kick on 1 and the "and" of 3, shuffled hats)
organ bass and subby "wobbly" basses (speed garage)
genres.producer_wants: An organ bass with a click; chopped vocals that can be pitched up 2-5 semitones; stabs with swing; a punchy kit with rim.
genres.sndrec_feel: Pitched-up vocal chops are what Sound Recorder's Increase Speed does: a real chipmunk from a real speed-up. Leave the artefacts in.

genres.name: Dubstep (UK and brostep)
genres.keys: Minor, Phrygian; often E or F minor; sparse
signature: sub bass and LFO wobble bass (UK), growl/"talking" basses (brostep)
genres.producer_wants: Wobbles locked to tempo (1/4, 1/8, triplets), a clean sub, growls with movement, impacts.
genres.sndrec_feel: Draw the wobble in the amplitude envelope; use macro N to change the repeat count of the buffer's last step (the rhythm of the chop).

genres.name: Hip-hop (boom bap)
genres.keys: Minor and jazz-derived; loops from soul and jazz records; chopped chords
signature: hard sampled drums from breaks, 12-bit grit (SP-1200, MPC60)
chopped soul/jazz samples, often slowed or sped up
filtered bass (low-passed sample) or upright bass
genres.producer_wants: Dusty drums that knock, chops with grit and swing, 12-bit colour, horn stabs.
genres.sndrec_feel: Sound Recorder IS a 1990s PC sampler: 8-bit 11 kHz sources and Increase/Decrease Speed round trips give SP-1200-like aliasing for free. Do not clean it up.

genres.name: Lo-fi hip-hop
genres.keys: Jazz chords: maj7, min9, 7#9; ii-V; often Db, Eb, F
signature: soft, side-chained drums with low-passed kicks
genres.producer_wants: Warm keys with tape wow, vinyl noise, soft kits, and a "study" mood with rain.
genres.sndrec_feel: Tape wow (v3 V) on a real Sound Recorder playback is the most honest lo-fi there is; the library's rain and room sounds make the bed.

genres.name: Trap
genres.keys: Minor, Phrygian and harmonic minor; dark bells and plucks; 808 carries the bass line
signature: long, tuned 808 kick-bass with glide and distortion
dark bells, plucks and flute loops
genres.producer_wants: An 808 that is in tune, long, with glide and saturation; bell/flute melodies; hats that roll.
genres.sndrec_feel: Make the 808 a slowed Windows boom: balloon<<< is an 808 tail. Glide is v3 mono.

genres.name: Synthwave and outrun
genres.keys: Minor (A, D, E minor); i-VI-III-VII; arpeggiated chords
genres.producer_wants: Chorus-wide pads, a gated snare, a tight 16th bass arp, a soaring lead.
genres.sndrec_feel: Echo plus a drawn envelope that cuts it is a gated reverb. Wide U and pan are the chorus.

sources.title: MusicTech: dreamy synths and retro drums (synthwave guide)

genres.name: Chillwave
genres.keys: Major 7th and add9; hazy, nostalgic; often a semitone off concert
signature: heavily filtered, washed-out synths and samples
genres.producer_wants: Warm, washed-out keys and pads that wobble; reverb-soaked vocal textures.
genres.sndrec_feel: Slow, echo and wow everything; prefer the XP startup family for the "summer" colour.

genres.name: Ambient
genres.keys: Major/lydian or static modal; long single chords
genres.producer_wants: Pads that evolve on their own; long releases; motion without rhythm; field recordings.
genres.sndrec_feel: Loops of different lengths are layers of different lengths: each recorder ends on its own. Grains (v3) let the XP startup become an endless cloud.

genres.name: Drone
genres.keys: One pitch or one chord; just intonation colour; fifths
genres.producer_wants: Infinite sustain, slow beating, overtones that move.
genres.sndrec_feel: LOOP-OSC builds 30 s buffers; held notes play to the end. Machines (hum, motors) are drones.

genres.name: IDM and glitch
genres.keys: Free; detuned bells, microtonal colour; melody from FM and toy sounds
signature: detuned bells, music boxes, toy sounds
genres.producer_wants: Glitches that are musical, stutters in time, unusual percussion, broken bells.
genres.sndrec_feel: Sound Recorder's editing commands are glitch tools: repeated @0CP stutters, Insert File splices, Delete Before/After cuts. Show them; the strip display shows the edit.

genres.name: Breakbeat and big beat
genres.keys: Blues and rock riffs, minor pentatonic; acid lines; one-chord riffs
genres.producer_wants: Fat breaks, distorted riffs, sirens, shout hits, big risers.
genres.sndrec_feel: Clip steps (+) are the distortion; the 3.x fanfare is the brass.

genres.name: Electro
genres.keys: Minor, often one key centre; robotic, staccato
genres.producer_wants: 808 kit, robotic voice, staccato bass, zaps.
genres.sndrec_feel: Use Microsoft Sam (in our XP image) for the robot voice once it is rendered to the disc.

genres.name: Downtempo and trip-hop
genres.keys: Minor; film-noir harmony; Dorian
signature: slow, heavy breakbeats with vinyl noise
genres.producer_wants: Cinematic strings, dusty Rhodes, dub bass, a noir lead.
genres.sndrec_feel: Slow down, add echo, keep the vinyl crumble in.

genres.name: Footwork and juke
genres.keys: Free; chopped samples set the key; 808 kicks played chromatically
signature: triplet and polyrhythmic hats and claps
genres.producer_wants: A kick that can be played chromatically, tight claps, chopped vocal loops.
genres.sndrec_feel: Kicks pitched by sample rate (no pitch-shifter): exactly what each recorder does.

genres.producer_wants: Glossy plastic sounds, pitched vocal stacks, distorted supersaws, bubbly perc.

genres.sndrec_feel: XP's glassy bells are FM-like already: print, default and xpding are the e-piano.

genres.keys: Pentatonic and modal; drones; just-intonation colour

genres.producer_wants: Breathy leads, bells, nature, and processed acoustic colour; calm and clean.

genres.keys: Major 6, maj7; Latin and lounge harmony
genres.producer_wants: Vibes, marimba, birdsong, gongs, island perc.
genres.sndrec_feel: Slow the birds down by octaves, the way exotica records did.

genres.name: Video-game chiptune

genres.producer_wants: Clean pulse leads with duty choices, triangle bass, noise drums, fast arps.
genres.sndrec_feel: LOOP-OSC buzzes ARE pulse waves made of a looped slice; a 3.11 8-bit source adds the grit.
